subject: How many starting values to give colext()?

messages.author: f4bebbdb3c5fcabc
messages.subject: How many starting values to give colext()?
parts:
As starting values for colext, would I have to give one for each year that I am modeling separately?
For instance, if I model 10 years, do I have to give 1 value for psi, 10 for gamma, 10 for epsilon and 1 or 10 for p? Also -  in that order?

I tried 4 (1 for psi, gamma, epsilon and p each), but got the error "Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = getHessian, ...) : 
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite"

I used the "simple" model:
fm1<-colext(psiformula = ~1, # first year occupancy
            gammaformula=~month-1, # colonization
            epsilonformula = ~month-1, # extinction
            pformula=~month-1, # detection
             data=occu_file,starts=c(0,0,0,0))

(I also tried this with non-zero start values but got the same error.

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: How many starting values to give colext()?
parts: If psi, p, gamma, epsilon were all modeled as ~1, there would be 4 parameters (and 4 starting values). With the monthly means parameterization as formulated here, you need 37: 1 for psi, and 12 for each of the other components of the model.

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: How many starting values to give colext()?
parts: Whoops, the above assumes all months are being considered, but more generally, you'll need one starting value for each monthly term as formulated.
